items.name: Kerala Ash Gourd Mung Olan
steps: Measure 850 ml (about 3 1/2 cups) water for Kerala Ash Gourd Mung Olan; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.
Cover the mung beans with at least three times their volume of cool water and soak for 30 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.
Simmer the soaked mung until it begins to soften. Maintain low heat for 9–11 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until the pulses crush easily against the side of the pot.
Slide in the ash-gourd batons without breaking them. Allow 3 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.

Grind the grated coconut with a ladle of hot cooking liquid and fold the pale cream into the tender vegetables. Work in 5 short pulses, pausing between them so the mixture stays cool and retains the intended texture.

Draw the pot from the heat, season gently, and perfume the surface with torn curry leaves and coconut oil. Wait 6 minutes, taste once the heat settles, and adjust only then before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Kerala Ash Gourd Mung Olan 6 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

Cook the pumpkin cubes with the crushed cumin until their edges are soft but their centers still hold shape. Maintain moderate heat for 9–11 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Add the peas and a smooth coconut paste. Keep the heat medium-low and work for 3 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.

Simmer quietly so the vegetables take up the creamy broth. Maintain gentle medium heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.
Turn off the flame before drizzling over the coconut oil and scattering the torn curry leaves. Keep the layer loose and even, with no pooled liquid, so every portion receives the same balance.
Rest Kerala Pumpkin and Pea Olan 3 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

ingredients.name: Chayote, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Measure 400 ml (about 1 3/4 cups) water for Karnataka Chayote Majjige Huli; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.
For Karnataka Chayote Majjige Huli, cover the chana dal with at least three times their volume of cool water and soak for 30 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.

Cook the chayote chunks with turmeric until tender enough to cut with the edge of a spoon. Maintain moderate heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Grind the soaked chana dal with coconut and cumin, simmer this paste around the vegetable. Work in 5 short pulses, pausing between them so the mixture stays cool and retains the intended texture.
Let it lose its raw taste. Allow 2 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.
Lower the heat before folding in the whisked yogurt. Keep the heat low and work for 1 minute so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Finish without boiling with mustard and curry leaves tempered in coconut oil. Wait 4 minutes, taste once the heat settles, and adjust only then before serving at the stated temperature.

items.name: Karnataka Green Bean Coconut Palya

ingredients.name: Green beans, cut on a fine diagonal

steps: Heat 70 ml (about 1/4 cup) water until vigorously boiling, then lower it to a bare simmer beside the main pot for measured additions.

Brown the split black gram in coconut oil and wait for the mustard to pop before adding turmeric and curry leaves. Use moderate heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until aromatic without scorching.
Toss in the diagonally cut beans with a splash of hot water. Keep the heat medium-low and work for 3 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Cover until they are tender but still green. Allow 2 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.
Cook off the remaining moisture, fold in the grated coconut. Maintain low heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until the aroma is rounded and the stated texture is reached.
Season the palya while it is hot. Wait 4 minutes, taste once the heat settles, and adjust only then before serving at the stated temperature.

items.name: Karnataka Beet Sesame Palya
steps: Set aside 60 ml (about 1/4 cup) freshly boiled water for Karnataka Beet Sesame Palya, reserving about 60 ml to correct the final consistency.
Crackle mustard and cumin in coconut oil. Use steady low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until aromatic without scorching.
Add the torn curry leaves without letting them scorch. Keep the heat moderate and work for 2 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Scatter in the coarse beet shreds, splash the pan with hot water. Keep the layer loose and even, with no pooled liquid, so every portion receives the same balance.
Cover until the raw crunch softens. Allow 2 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.
Uncover, toss with the ground sesame. Keep the heat low and work for 1 minute so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Cook until the palya is moist but no liquid pools beneath it. Maintain steady low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until the aroma is rounded and the stated texture is reached.
Rest Karnataka Beet Sesame Palya 6 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

steps: Complete the listed rinsing, cutting, and draining for the cabbage, green peas, and fresh coconut before heating the pan; keep the pieces even so they reach doneness together.
Pop the mustard in coconut oil. Allow 3 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.
Add the slit chili and curry leaves for a short aromatic burst. Keep the heat low and work for 3 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Tumble in the cabbage and peas, cover for a few minutes. Allow 2 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.
Let the vegetables soften in their own steam. Maintain a steady steam for 6–8 minutes and check until the aroma is rounded and the stated texture is reached.
Remove the lid while some bite remains, stir through the coconut and salt. Keep the heat medium-low and work for 2 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Serve the palya promptly. Wait 5 minutes, taste once the heat settles, and adjust only then before serving at the stated temperature.

items.name: Karnataka Methi Brown Rice Bath
steps: Prepare 700 ml (about 3 cups) hot water before starting Karnataka Methi Brown Rice Bath; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.
Cover the brown rice with at least three times their volume of cool water and soak for 30 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.

Soften the chopped fenugreek leaves in ghee with cumin until their raw bitterness mellows. Allow 3 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.

Stir in the soaked rice, peas, coriander, and turmeric, coating every grain in the green mixture. Keep the heat steady low and work for 3 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Pour in hot water, cover. Allow 2 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.
Cook gently until the rice is tender. Maintain medium-low heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Rest the bath before fluffing and seasoning. Wait 4 minutes, taste once the heat settles, and adjust only then before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Karnataka Methi Brown Rice Bath 7 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

steps: Complete the listed rinsing, cutting, and draining for the sorghum grains, lemon juice, and peanuts before heating the pan; keep the pieces even so they reach doneness together.

Toast the split black gram in sesame oil. Use steady low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until aromatic without scorching.
Add mustard, peanuts, turmeric, and curry leaves. Keep the heat moderate and work for 1 minute so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Fold the hot tempering into the sorghum, take the pan off the flame. Keep the heat medium-low and work for 1 minute so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Mix in the lemon juice and salt. Keep the heat gentle medium and work for 2 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.

steps: Complete the listed rinsing, cutting, and draining for the brown rice, fresh coconut, and sesame seeds before heating the pan; keep the pieces even so they reach doneness together.
Loosen the tender brown rice with a fork and keep it covered while the flavoring is prepared. Use moderate heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until aromatic without scorching.
Brown the cashew pieces in ghee, add cumin and curry leaves. Use medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until aromatic without scorching.
Stir in the coconut just until fragrant. Keep the heat gentle medium and work for 2 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Fold the warm mixture and ground sesame through the rice, season. Use low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until aromatic without scorching.

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into cubes

steps: Measure 520 ml (about 2 1/4 cups) water for Karnataka Pumpkin Peanut Gojju; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.
Sputter mustard and fenugreek in sesame oil. Allow 2 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.
Turn the pumpkin cubes through the aromatic fat. Allow 2 minutes for this stage and use the texture and aroma cues, rather than the clock alone, to decide when to continue.

Add the diluted tamarind and simmer until the pumpkin yields while retaining its shape. Maintain gentle medium heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Stir in the coarse peanuts and grated jaggery, reduce the gojju to a clinging sauce. Maintain low heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.

ingredients.name: Ridge gourd, peeled in stripes and diced

steps: Heat 850 ml (about 3 1/2 cups) water until vigorously boiling, then lower it to a bare simmer beside the main pot for measured additions.

Add the diced ridge gourd and slit chili. Keep the heat medium-low and work for 2 minutes so the addition disperses without breaking the main pieces.
Simmer until the vegetable becomes soft and the tovve thickens. Maintain gentle medium heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the aroma is rounded and the stated texture is reached.
Bloom cumin and curry leaves in ghee, stir this tempering through the dal. Use low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until aromatic without scorching.

items.name: Karnataka Spinach Mung Bassaru
steps: Prepare 1050 ml (about 4 1/2 cups) hot water before starting Karnataka Spinach Mung Bassaru; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.
For Karnataka Spinach Mung Bassaru, cover the mung beans with at least three times their volume of cool water and soak for 40 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.
Cook the soaked mung until tender, add the spinach. Maintain medium-low heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until the pulses crush easily against the side of the pot.
Drain off most of the green cooking broth into a second pot. Let it drain for 1 minutes without pressing harder than the recipe's texture requires.

Simmer the reserved broth with chopped tomato, cumin, and pepper until it becomes a fragrant, light saaru. Maintain low heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.
Mash the remaining beans and greens coarsely, season both preparations. Wait 3 minutes, taste once the heat settles, and adjust only then before serving at the stated temperature.
Finish the broth with warm ghee before serving them together. Use moderate heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until aromatic without scorching.
